rules.sentence: As there is no curative therapy for Jacobsen syndrome, prognosis is often determined by the severity of cardiac or hematologic disease.
There is a 20% risk of mortality within the first 2 years of life, often due to complications of cardiac defects or after high-risk cardiothoracic surgery.
The overall life expectancy is largely unknown, although the oldest documented patients have reached 45 years of age.[2]
Jacobsen syndrome presents unique risks for cardiopulmonary bypass and cardiothoracic surgery that should be carefully managed.[23]
